title: Follow a clue from one file to another
summary: Two notes sit in one folder. Find which one holds the book title and which one points the way.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder.
features: Use the project file list and ask the helper to read two files.
roles: Follow a note to a mail report.
Find the file that holds a meeting date.
Find the title shown on a home screen.
prompt: Make title.txt say Harbor Notes. Make route.txt say Open title.txt first. Read both. Tell me where the title lives, which file points there, and whether either gives a date. Keep just these two files.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Open each file from the list of edits. Read its one line out loud.
steps.help: title.txt says Harbor Notes. The other note points to title.txt.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Ask the helper which line gives the date. Look in both files for that line.
steps.help: If a date turns up, ask the helper to quote it. Reopen the two files and compare.

check: title.txt says Harbor Notes. The other note points to title.txt.
Neither file gives a date. A good answer says it is missing.

title: Fix one title and keep its neighbors
summary: Change a spelling mistake on one line of a list. The other lines need to stay in place.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder.
features: Read the old and new lines in the change view.
roles: Fix a label on one mail rule.
Correct one folder name on a list.
Fix one game title in a menu.
prompt: Create catalog.txt with these three lines in order: Dock Notes, Dock Notse, Dock Notes Archive. Use a separate line for each. Stop so I can check the file.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Read and count all three lines. Ask the helper to fix the spelling on line two only.
steps.help: Before the edit, the second line says Dock Notse. After it, the second line says Dock Notes.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Open the changed file. Count how many lines now say exactly Dock Notes. Check the last line too.
steps.help: If one line disappears, ask for the original order and both copies. Check the whole list again.

check: Before the edit, the second line says Dock Notse. After it, the second line says Dock Notes.
There are two copies of Dock Notes. Line three still says Dock Notes Archive.

title: Build a quiz card you can turn over
summary: Make a tiny page with a question on one side and a hidden answer you can reveal.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder.
features: Make an HTML file and open it in a browser.
roles: Hide or show details for a mailbox.
Reveal the answer on a training slide.
Make a playable quiz card.
prompt: Build index.html. Show Harbor Quiz and the question Which boat leaves first? Add a Show answer button. Hide Dawn Ferry at first. The button reveals it and changes to Hide answer. A second click hides it again. Put the page and its script in this one file.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Open index.html in your browser. Read the question before touching the button.
steps.help: At first the question is visible and Dawn Ferry is hidden.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Click twice. Watch both the answer and the button. Refresh the page.
steps.help: If the words change on the button but the answer stays put, ask the helper to change both on each click.

check: At first the question is visible and Dawn Ferry is hidden.
One click reveals Dawn Ferry. The next hides it. Refresh starts with the answer hidden.

title: Count a real zero in a messy table
summary: One row has zero minutes. Another has no time at all. Find out why only one belongs in the count.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder. Install Python 3 if the computer cannot run Python files.
features: Read a table saved as text, then run a short Python script.
roles: Count mailboxes that had zero errors.
Add times from a meeting log.
Keep a zero-point round on a scorecard.
prompt: Make input.csv with the heading ID,minutes and rows A,15 then B,0 then C, then D,oops. Write summarize.py in Python 3. Count rows with numbers, including zero. Add their minutes. List the IDs of skipped rows. Use the tools built into Python and run the file.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Open input.csv. Find B and C. Ask the helper to run python3 summarize.py and show the printed result.
steps.help: A and B count. Their total is 15. The skipped IDs are C and D.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Change C, to C,6 and save. Run the same file again.
steps.help: If only A counts at first, ask the helper to check for an empty cell before turning the text into a number.

check: A and B count. Their total is 15. The skipped IDs are C and D.
Three rows now count. Total minutes are 21. Only D is skipped.

title: Sort scores as numbers
summary: A computer can put 10 ahead of 2 when it sorts words. Teach a scoreboard to sort numbers instead.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder.
features: Read a sorting rule in JavaScript and try the result in a browser.
roles: Sort mailbox sizes from small to large.
Sort a team's list of wait times.
Sort game scores and keep tied players.
prompt: Create sort.html with a Sort button. Start with the three text values 10, 2 and 0. On click, show what JavaScript sort() returns with no extra rule. Leave this first version as it is until I test it. Provide an editable input so I can repeat the sort with different numbers.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Open sort.html. Click Sort. Read the three numbers from left to right.
steps.help: The first version gives 0, 10, 2. It has sorted by the first written digit.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Ask for a number sort that keeps repeats. Test the three numbers again. Then put in 10, 2, 2, 0 and try Sort.
steps.help: If the second 2 vanishes, ask for a sorted list that keeps every entry. Count the four items.

check: The first version gives 0, 10, 2. It has sorted by the first written digit.
The fixed results are 0, 2, 10 and then 0, 2, 2, 10.

writeYourOwn.goal: Show why a scoreboard put 10 ahead of 2, then fix it.
writeYourOwn.given: The starting values are the text labels 10, 2 and 0. Add another 2 for a second test.
writeYourOwn.compare: Does your request preserve the broken first result long enough to see it?

title: Open an old score and a new score
summary: Teach one reader where two versions of a game save their points.

features: Use Python tests to check two kinds of saved game file.
roles: Open a report saved by an older mail tool.
Read two versions of a shared form.
Open scores saved before a game update.
prompt: Plan a Python reader for these three records: {"version":1,"points":7}, {"version":2,"score":0}, {"version":3,"score":99}. The first version uses points. The second uses score. Raise ValueError for an unknown version. Show the planned tests before writing files.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Read the plan. Ask for reader.py and test_reader.py. Ask the helper to run python3 -m unittest -v. Find a passing test for each known version.
steps.help: The old record gives 7. The newer record gives 0.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Add one test for version 2 with no score field. Keep the test for version 3 and run the checks again.
steps.help: If zero fails, check whether the score field exists. If a new version passes, check the version number before reading its fields.

check: The old record gives 7. The newer record gives 0.
The unknown version and the version with a missing score both give a clear error.

title: Keep a help desk open past midnight
summary: Build a clock rule for a desk that opens at ten at night and closes at two in the morning.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder. Install Python 3 if the computer cannot run Python files.
features: Use a table of clock times to test a Python rule.
roles: Display when a mail help desk is open.
Show coverage hours on a staff page.
Make a game shop that opens overnight.
prompt: Plan is_open(hour, minute) in Python. The desk opens at 22:00 and closes at 02:00. Count the opening minute. Treat the closing minute as closed. Times use a 24-hour clock. Raise ValueError for a bad hour or minute. Show a test table first.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Ask for the code and tests. Read the table at 21:59, 22:00, 00:00, 01:59, 02:00 and noon. Run the tests.
steps.help: In order the answers are closed, open, open, open, closed and closed.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Try the made-up times 24:00 and 01:60. Look for an error for each one.
steps.help: If midnight shows closed, check both pieces of the shift. Check the minute just before and exactly at closing.

check: In order the answers are closed, open, open, open, closed and closed.
Both bad times raise ValueError. They never show up as ordinary closed hours.

title: Follow a report past an empty page

roles: Read all pages of a mail report.
Collect every page of a shared list.
Load another page of game results.
prompt: Build a Python test with pretend pages. Start at p1. Its value list is ["A"] and its @odata.nextLink is p2. Page p2 has [] and links to p3. Page p3 has ["C"] and no link. Record every page you ask for. Stop with an error if a link repeats. Keep the test on this computer.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Run the test. Compare the page log with the list of letters collected.
steps.help: It visits p1, p2 and p3 in order. The result is A, C.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Have p3 point back to p2. Run again and read the last line in the log.
steps.help: If C is gone, ask the helper to stop when there is no next link. An empty list alone is not the end.

check: It visits p1, p2 and p3 in order. The result is A, C.
The reader reports a loop before asking for p2 a second time.
sources: Microsoft Learn · paging through Graph results

title: Open and close the rules with a keyboard
summary: Let someone read the rules and return to the game using only keys.

features: Move through a rules box with the Tab, Enter and Escape keys.
roles: Read mail-report hints with the keyboard.
Open help in a staff form.
Add accessible rules to a game.
prompt: Build dialog.html. Add a Rules button. Enter opens a box with a heading, the words Two players take turns, and a Close button. Move the keyboard highlight to Close. Keep it inside the box until Escape or Close shuts it. Return the highlight to Rules.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Open the page. Press Tab until Rules is highlighted. Press Enter. Use Tab and Shift with Tab to see where the highlight goes.
steps.help: The box opens. You can read its rule. The keyboard highlight reaches Close and stays in the open box.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Press Escape. Check the highlight. Open Rules again. This time activate Close with the keyboard.
steps.help: If the highlight disappears, ask the helper to remember the opening button and focus it when the box closes.

check: The box opens. You can read its rule. The keyboard highlight reaches Close and stays in the open box.
Both ways put the highlight back on Rules. While the box is closed, you cannot tab to its Close button.

writeYourOwn.goal: Make a Rules panel that works with a keyboard.
writeYourOwn.given: Start on Rules. Try Enter, Tab, Escape and Close without touching the screen.
writeYourOwn.compare: Look for a check that the keyboard highlight returns to the button that opened the box.

title: Update a book that works offline

features: Use a local web server and a browser helper that saves pages for offline reading.
roles: Pack a read-only mail checklist for a trip.
Save a training page for an offline class.
Update an iPad book without losing its offline pages.
prompt: Build a little book on localhost with index.html, chapter.txt saying edition A, and sw.js. This last file is a browser helper. Have it save the page and chapter for offline use. Show Ready offline once it can serve this page. Remove only this book’s old saved copies when a new edition takes over. Give me a command to serve the folder.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Run the given command. Open its local address. Wait for Ready offline. Take the browser offline and reload this same page.
steps.help: Edition A still opens. The page can read its chapter without a network connection.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Go online. Ask the helper to change the chapter to edition B and the name of its saved copy. Close old book tabs, reopen online and wait. Go offline again and reload.
steps.help: If A returns, close all old book tabs. Open online, wait for the new helper to take over, then test offline again.

check: Edition A still opens. The page can read its chapter without a network connection.
The reader now shows B offline. In the browser storage view the old copy of this book is gone.

title: Count each score slip once

features: Use a local database and two separate writers to check repeated scores.
roles: Count each mail event once.
Avoid double counting forms sent twice.
Keep a score slip from adding points twice.
prompt: Use Python and a temporary SQLite database. Store each score ID just once. Enter A,+40 and B,+40. Send A,+40 again. Reject a repeat ID with a changed amount. Also send C,+10 from two separate connections at the same time. Have the database enforce the one-ID rule.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Ask to see the stored rows after the repeat and again after both copies of C arrive. Run the tests on a fresh database.
steps.help: The repeat leaves A and B, total 80. After C there are three rows and the total is 90.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Repeat the two-connection test on fresh data. Then try A,+41 against the finished database.
steps.help: If the total reaches 100, ask for a rule in the database that blocks a second row with the same ID. Test both connections again.

check: The repeat leaves A and B, total 80. After C there are three rows and the total is 90.
The tool flags the change. A still has 40 points and the total stays 90.

title: Find which setting wins
summary: Stack three sets of settings. The top set can turn an option off or choose zero as a limit.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder. Install Python 3 if the computer cannot run Python files.
features: Read three groups of choices and show which group set each value.
roles: Explain where a mail warning limit came from.
Check which team setting took effect.
Let a player turn reminders off.
prompt: In Python, start with reminders=true and limit=10. The site sets limit=5. The user sets reminders=false and limit=0. Use the last set that actually names a setting. Show its value and where it came from. Reject a named value of null and unknown setting names. Keep the input lists unchanged.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Run the first example. Remove limit from the user settings and run again. Then remove the site limit too.
steps.help: At first the user gives false and 0. Removing the user limit gives 5 from the site. Removing both gives 10 from the defaults.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Try reminders=false with a misspelled setting called typo_lim. In another test, set limit to null. Look at the original lists after each run.
steps.help: If 0 becomes 5, ask whether the key is present, instead of asking whether its value is positive.

check: At first the user gives false and 0. Removing the user limit gives 5 from the site. Removing both gives 10 from the defaults.
Both bad inputs raise an error. The original settings still match what you put in.

title: Teach two app versions to share a score
summary: Find a way to save points that both an old game and a new game can read.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder. Install Python 3 if the computer cannot run Python files.
features: Make two readers try the same files, like testing two keys on one lock.
roles: Change a mail report while older readers still use it.
Update a shared form in small steps.
Keep old saved games working.
prompt: In Python make an old reader that looks for points. Make a new reader that accepts points or score and rejects different values when both appear. Build an old writer that saves only points. Build a second writer that saves both fields with the same value. Test both readers with both writers for 0 and -7.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Draw two reader columns and two writer rows. Mark each box after the helper runs its tests.
steps.help: All four pairs read both 0 and -7 correctly.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Add a writer that saves only score. Try both readers. Then give them a record with points=3 and score=4. Ask which readers should be updated first.
steps.help: If both readers pass everything, inspect the test that uses only score. The old reader must notice its missing points field.

check: All four pairs read both 0 and -7 correctly.

The old reader rejects the score-only file. The new reader accepts it. For points=3 and score=4, the old reader returns 3 and the new reader rejects the disagreement. Update readers before switching writers.

title: Count overlapping outage minutes once
summary: Two teams report the same outage. Combine their time blocks without counting the overlap twice.
requires: Open Antigravity on a computer. Use an empty practice folder. Install Python 3 if the computer cannot run Python files.
features: Put overlapping time blocks on the same clock and measure their combined length.
roles: Measure combined mail downtime.
Read service windows on a team calendar.
Count time spent playing without overlap.
prompt: Use Python and UTC times on January 1–2, 2027. A runs from Jan 1 23:50 to Jan 2 00:10. On Jan 2, B runs 00:05–00:20, C runs 00:20–00:25, and D runs 00:08–00:09. Count each minute of downtime once. End times mark when service is back. Accept an interval of zero minutes. Reject an end earlier than its start.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt into the project chat. Read the proposed steps. Draw the four lines on a time strip. Ask the helper for the total. Shuffle the input, repeat A, and try D with the same start and end.
steps.help: The combined stretch is 35 minutes. Shuffle, repeats and an empty stretch add zero minutes.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Add Jan 2 01:00 to 01:02. Then feed the tool one interval with the end earlier than its start.
steps.help: If the total is too large, merge overlapping blocks before adding their lengths. Check that C starts just when B ends.

check: The combined stretch is 35 minutes. Shuffle, repeats and an empty stretch add zero minutes.
The separated two minutes raise the total to 37. The reversed interval gets a clear error.

title: Restart an import where it stopped

features: Stop and restart a Python job using a saved place marker.

Resume reading a file of test survey rows.
Restore a score list after a broken import.
prompt: Build a local Python importer with temporary SQLite. Input is R1,+8 then R2,-3 then R3,+5. Save each row and its place marker together so both are kept or neither is. Add a practice switch to stop just after saving row two. Resume, then run the whole file again. Reject repeats with a changed amount.

steps.title: Open the practice folder
steps.text: In Antigravity on a computer, open a new project with just one empty practice folder.
steps.help: Look for the folder name in the chat header. If you see another project, switch folders first.

steps.title: Ask the helper

steps.help: After the stop there are two rows, total 5, marker 2. After resuming there are three rows, total 10, marker 3.
